en: "I have no intention of killing you."{w}
"I know that already, dammit!!{w}I'm asking why it's bitter melon from top to bottom! Well?! HUH?!!"{w}
"We do not have any cooking utensils.{w}When I tried making a new dish, they all broke."{w}{p}"And with the utensils I had left, this was all I could make."{w}
note: Editorial: Tris speaks without contractions (voice of slice_024).

en: "This is a mining town, isn't it?! Then get somebody to make them for you!"{w}
note: Editorial: source is an imperative to Tris; made a direct order.

en: "Everyone is busy with their work.{w}So I asked the adventurers over there to go to the Scorching Castle."{w}
note: Editorial: 'those adventurers there' -> 'the adventurers over there' (flow).

en: "Tch, what kind of answer is that? ...Fine, whatever.{w}You there, sorry, but please take on the request. Whenever you have time is fine. My apologies."{w}
"By the way~{w}if the utensils do not come in time, the next meal will be a full course of bitter melon again~"{w}
note: Elongation marks rendered as '~'. Editorial: Tris speaks without contractions (voice of slice_024). Missing article restored; 'too' -> 'again' (next meal as well).

en: "Hey, you! What are you standing around gawking for?!!{w}Go now! Go right now! Go on the double!!{w}Hurry up, you dawdler! Slowpoooke!!"{w}
note: Tarmeet switches to rude singular omae for the party; kept as 'you' with singular insults as in the source. Editorial: 'Go at a dead run' -> 'Go on the double' (spoken).

en: "You brought them. That is amazing!{w}These look like they can stand up to any kind of cooking!{w}Thank you very much!"{w}
note: Editorial: Tris speaks without contractions (voice of slice_024). 'With these, I think they' had an unclear 'they'.

en:
"Well done, adventurers!
Now I'm free of bitter melon!!{w}This is my thanks. Take it."{w}
"All right, I will make even more delicious food for everyone!!{w}...Like marinated bitter melon~"{w}
note: Editorial: Tris speaks without contractions (voice of slice_024).

en: "Okay, line up, line up. I would like you to line up.{w}No cutting in line."{w}{p}"Hello, everyone.{w}Tris has been in top form ever since."{w}
note: Tris refers to itself by name here; kept third person. Editorial: page 1 has the same Japanese as slice_024 5422 page 1; English aligned to it (lead note).

en: Tarmeet's Voice
note: Pattern of the glossary entry 'Jera's Voice'.

en:
"GYAAAAAHHH!?
Bitter melon on my plate AGAAAIN!?"{w}
You thought you heard someone scream...{w}

"Tris's delicious meals~
Would you all like to have a taste too?"{w}
note: Music note -> '~'.

en: Who will you talk to?
note: Choice prompt: Jera or Jeratan.

en: Jera

"Welcome!{w}Oh, how unusual! You're not from Gandra, are you?{w}I'm Jera. Where are you all from?"{w}{p}"...Uh-huh, uh-huh.{w}The Decree from Bistel?
Wow, so there are still adventurers taking it on!"{w}{p}"Oh, I don't mean that in a weird way.
Sorry, sorry. It must be tough for you."{w}{p}"If you like, take a rest in my shop.
I can at least make you some tea~"{w}
"Jeratan wantth to be introduthed too!"{w}
note: Jeratan's babyish lisp (deshu/kudashai) rendered with a light s->th lisp on a few words per line.

en: "Oh, sorry, sorry!{w}That's Jeratan, hanging on the wall over there!"{w}
Jeratan
"I'm Jeratan.{w}Pleathe play with me."{w}

"Jeratan is a magic puppet that Tarmeet made, using me as the model."{w}{p}"If you give Jeratan sweets and win at rock-paper-scissors, you'll get rare Tarot cards handed down in a land far to the east."{w}{p}"The more precious the sweets, the better the Tarot you get, so play with Jeratan if you like!"{w}
note: Jeratan's gender unknown: no pronouns, name repeated. Editorial: clumsy apposition reordered (first sentence only).

en: "Eastern culture is so elegant, don't you think?{w}I got totally hooked on it and even redid the shop's interior!"{w}{p}"Lately I've been looking for even rarer things, so I've been getting on good terms with Saimar too.{w}A port town really does get a different flow of goods!"{w}
"By the way, you guys..."{w}{p}"What do you think when you look at me?{w}Is there anything strange about me?{w}...Ah, besides the Eastern clothes. Like... overall?"{w}
note: wasou (Japanese-style dress) -> 'the Eastern clothes', matching the game's 'East' = Japan analogue.

en: Does anything seem off?
"Aww... And I'm trying so hard..."{w}{p}"So which part looks weird?{w}Here? Or here? Maybe over here...?{w}Don't just stay quiet, tell me... You're so mean."{w}
"Really?{w}Eee, I'm happy even if it's just flattery!"{w}{p}"Huh? What am I talking about?{w}Geez! Don't ask such tactless questions.{w}Hee hee~"{w}

"I think I've collected a fair number of things from the East, but..."{w}{p}"They're kind of meh. There's nothing that makes me go 'This is it!'{w}You know, real treasures, or a master-forged blade."{w}{p}"You're adventurers, right?{w}If you don't mind, could you go find the items written here for me?"{w}
note: gyoumono = blade by a master smith.

en:
The note you were handed listed the names of four items:
'Hundred Bamboo Edge', 'Chihaya Benizakura', 'Yasha Princess', 'Mikaboshi'{w}
note: Item names follow the glossary (Elminage III spellings: Hundred Bamboo Edge, Chihaya Benizakura, Yasha Princess, Mikaboshi). Accuracy: replaced stale note that said they were romanized; en unchanged.

en: "I don't expect a top-grade katana or anything, obviously, but something like the Chihaya should be fairly easy to get hold of, and, well, I'd kind of like to try wearing it, you know?"{w}
note: 'Chihaya' = short for Chihaya Benizakura (a chihaya is a robe-like garment).

en: "Please!{w}If you gather them all, I'll throw in some sweet buns on the house at least! Okay?"{w}
note: amashoku (a sweet bun sold in Jera's shop, see slice_026 5667) -> 'sweet buns'; replace if an item-list name exists.

en: "Thanks for all your hard work. Won't you stay for some tea?"{w}
"That katana... could it be...{w}the Hundred Bamboo Edge?"{w}
"That robe... could it be...{w}the Chihaya Benizakura?"{w}
"That spear... could it be...{w}the Yasha Princess?"{w}
"That katana... could it be...{w}the Mikaboshi?"{w}
"Amazing... You got every single one...!{w}I can't believe it... Ahh..."{w}
Jera gazes at the items you gathered, letting out a soft sigh.{w}She looks very happy.{w}

"For someone like me...{w}What do I do, I'm so happy...!{w}This is the first time anyone's done so much for me..."{w}{p}"Since you worked this hard for me, I have to thank you properly.{w}What should I do..."{w}{p}"I know! I feel like I'd come across even rarer treasures if I stuck with you guys, so I'll register as an adventurer too!"{w}
"I'll sign up at the Training Hall in Bistel, so don't be shy about calling on me!"{w}
{0E} *  Jera has registered at the Training Hall  * {0F}{w}
"That... is it for me?"{w}
note: Which item is offered is not shown in the script (likely one of the four, after recruitment).

en: Give it to her?
"Really? Thank you!!"{w}
"R-right, of course! ...Sorry."{w}

"Later, after I close up shop...
want me to show you how I look in the Chihaya Benizakura?{w}Ufufu."{w}
note: Editorial: hiragana ufufu = 'Ufufu' (review_notes convention).

en: "Do you know the story of the Yasha Princess?"{w}
note: Here Yasha-hime is the legend's figure the spear is named after; glossary spelling kept. Editorial: article added, as in 5567.

en: "They say the Yasha Princess suffered from a one-sided love, and in the end burned up together with the one she loved in the flames of her passion, until they were both ash."{w}{p}"It's sad, but it's a lovely story, isn't it?{w}A great love you'd stake your life on... I can't help longing for that..."{w}
note: hime = princess, so 'she'; the beloved's gender unstated -> 'the one she loved'. Editorial: article added, as in 5567/5588.

en: "Maybe I should become a yasha too?{w}Hee hee..."{w}
note: yasha = demon (yaksha); lower-case common noun echoing the name.

en:
"Later, after I close up shop...
will you come see me in the Chihaya Benizakura?"{w}{p}"You went to the trouble of getting it for me, so I want to look cute in it. Okay?"{w}
"Jeratan, I'm home!{w}Were you a good kid while I was away?"{w}
"Jeratan ith alwayth a good kid!"{w}
"Of course you are!{w}Here, I brought you a souvenir!"{w}
"Wha--!?{w}What'th that thweet?!{w}I've never theen one before!?"{w}
"It's been a while, so let's eat it together!"{w}

"Ith that the thweet you thaid you wanted to find on thith trip --
the thweetheart tart?!"{w}
note: PUN ADAPTED: source rabu-ro-manjuu = Jeratan mishearing 'love romance' (rabu romansu) as a manju bun. Rendered as 'sweetheart' misheard as 'sweetheart tart'. Literal fallback: 'love-romance bun'. Same choice in 5608-5624. Editorial: lead rule for Jeratan: th-lisp on common s-words; 'Jeratan' only where the source has jeratan, I/me where the subject is dropped.

en: "Pfft!? A-a sweetheart... tart!?{w}Jeratan, don't spring that on me out of nowhere!{w}This isn't that! Ahahaha!"{w}
note: See 5606 pun note.

en: "Mmh?{w}Did I thay thomething weird?"{w}
"You didn't, you didn't, but...{w}Hehehe, t-tart...{w}Ahahaha! Hngh, bwahahaha!!"{w}
note: Jera repeats the bun part (manjuu) -> 'tart'.

en:
"Hmph! Jeratan wantth to eat a thweetheart tart too,
the kind that'th thweet, and thour, and a little bitter!"{w}{p}"Thtop laughing and go find one, pleathe!{w}Keeping it all to yourthelf ith not fair!!"{w}
note: Addressed to Jera (she is the one laughing). Editorial: lead rule for Jeratan: th-lisp on common s-words; 'Jeratan' only where the source has jeratan, I/me where the subject is dropped.

en:
"Ahahaha!
S-sorry! Hehehe!!"{w}

"You're right,
I'd like to find a sweetheart tart too."{w}
note: Double meaning (romance) kept as in source.

en:
"...I feel like I could find one
if I were with you...{w}Or would I not be good enough?"{w}
note: Jera switches to singular kimi: aimed at one party member (the 'you').

en:
"Just kidding!
Heh, I put you on the spot, didn't I? Sorry."{w}

"??? ...I don't really underthtand, but
hurry up and find it, pleathe.{w}...The thweetheart tart~"{w}
note: Music note -> '~'.

en: "Pfft!! Hngh... hehehe!!"{w}

"Hey! What'th tho funnyyy?!!
Hmph, hmph!!"{w}
note: Editorial: lead rule for Jeratan: th-lisp on common s-words; 'Jeratan' only where the source has jeratan, I/me where the subject is dropped. Row had no lisp although the source lisps (deshuka).

en: "I'll make thome tea!"{w}
Jera
Jeratan
Talk to Jeratan
Play with Jeratan

"You'll play with Jeratan?!
Yaaaay!!{w}Then firtht, give me a thweet, pleathe!"{w}{p}"If you give me thweetth Jeratan liketh,{w}your chanthe of getting a good Tarot when you win will be higher!!"{w}
note: Mid-sentence {w} kept at the same cut. Editorial: lead rule for Jeratan: th-lisp on common s-words; 'Jeratan' only where the source has jeratan, I/me where the subject is dropped.

en: "Huh?! You won't play?{w}You won't even give me a thweet?!{w}Even though I made tea and everything?!"{w}

"Thniff... Y-you're mean!!
Waaaaah!!"{w}
note: Editorial: lead rule for Jeratan: th-lisp on common s-words; 'Jeratan' only where the source has jeratan, I/me where the subject is dropped. The source lisps the sniffle itself (gushu).

en:
"Ooh!?{w}Wh-what ith that
thwirly rolled-up thweet?!"{w}
note: Editorial: lead rule for Jeratan: th-lisp on common s-words; 'Jeratan' only where the source has jeratan, I/me where the subject is dropped.

'Best treatment' = Jeratan will offer a better prize (cf. slice_026 5655). Editorial: lead rule for Jeratan: th-lisp on common s-words; 'Jeratan' only where the source has jeratan, I/me where the subject is dropped.

en: "Munch munch...{w}I've never eaten anything like thith!?{w}There really are yummy thweetth out there in the world!"{w}
